title: AlexsLemonade/morphport pipeline parameters
description: Downstream analysis of Cell Painting data to prepare for the PCCMA portal

input_output_options.title: Input/output options
input_output_options.description: Define where the pipeline should find input data and save output data.

publish_optional.description: Publish intermediate pipeline outputs, such as partitioned parquet files.
publish_optional.help_text: By default, intermediate outputs (e.g. from PARTITION_CONDITIONS) are not published to the output directory. Set this flag to publish them, which is useful for debugging. Automatically enabled by the 'debug' profile.

input.description: Path to comma-separated file containing information about the samples in the experiment.
input.help_text: You will need to create a design file with information about the samples in your experiment before running the pipeline. Use this parameter to specify its location. It has to be a comma-separated file with 3 columns, and a header row.

outdir.description: The output directory where the results will be saved. You have to use absolute paths to storage on Cloud infrastructure.

email.help_text: Set this parameter to your e-mail address to get a summary e-mail with details of the run sent to you when the workflow exits. If set in your user config file (`~/.nextflow/config`) then you don't need to specify this on the command line for every run.

processing_options.title: Processing options
processing_options.description: Parameters related to the general processing of the data.

platemap_well_column.description: Column name in the input samplesheet that contains the well identifiers.
platemap_well_column.help_text: The pipeline uses the values in this column to match the samplesheet to the plate parquet files. The values in this column should correspond to the 'Metadata_Well' column in the plate parquet files. This is typically a column that describes the well position on the plate, such as 'well_position' or 'well_id'.

analysis_groups_file.description: Path to a YAML (or JSON) file specifying how partitions should be grouped for downstream analysis.
analysis_groups_file.help_text: Defines named groupings of the platemap metadata, at the cell and/or well level. If not provided, all plates in a project are analyzed as a single group per level. See docs/analysis_groups_format.md for the file format and assets/analysis_groups_example.yaml for an example.

random_seed.description: Seed for stochastic steps in the pipeline (e.g., PCA, UMAP).

cosmicqc_filter_file.description: Path to JSON file specifying coSMicQC filter conditions and z-score thresholds.
cosmicqc_filter_file.help_text: Each entry in the JSON array defines a named condition with a dict of CellProfiler feature names to z-score thresholds. Positive thresholds flag cells above the z-score; negative thresholds flag cells below. Cells failing any condition are removed. Defaults to the reference thresholds bundled in assets/cosmicqc_filter_settings.json.

edge_well_filter.description: Whether to exclude wells on the border of the plate before coSMicQC filtering. Use 'off' to keep all wells, 'on' to drop edge wells, or 'both' to carry both edge-included and edge-excluded datasets through the rest of the pipeline.
edge_well_filter.help_text:
This filter assumes that all wells in a plate are filled with media, and will exclude only the plate edges. If there are empty wells on the plate, this filtering may not be sufficient.
Results from edge well filtering onward are published in an 'edge_wells_included' ('off') or 'edge_wells_excluded' ('on') subdirectory of each step's output directory. In 'both' mode, both subdirectories are created and downstream analysis groups are kept separate for each variant.

pycytominer_aggregate_operation.description: Aggregation function to use when summarising per-cell data to well-level profiles.

pycytominer_normalize_method_cell.description: Normalization method applied to cell-level profiles. Use 'none' to skip normalization.

pycytominer_normalize_method_well.description: Normalization method applied to well-level profiles. Use 'none' to skip normalization.

pycytominer_normalize_samples.description: Reference population for fitting the normalizer. Use 'all' to fit on all samples, or a pandas query string to fit on a subset (e.g. "Metadata_treatment == 'DMSO'").

feature_select_operations.description: Comma-separated list of pycytominer feature_select operations to apply per analysis group. Valid values: variance_threshold, correlation_threshold, drop_na_columns, blocklist, drop_outliers, noise_removal.

feature_select_na_cutoff.description: Maximum fraction of rows that may be NaN before a feature column is dropped by the drop_na_columns operation.

feature_select_corr_threshold.description: Correlation threshold for the correlation_threshold feature selection operation. Feature pairs with absolute correlation above this value are deduplicated.

feature_select_corr_method.description: Correlation method for the correlation_threshold feature selection operation. Valid values: pearson, spearman, kendall, with pearson the default.

feature_select_freq_cut.description: Frequency cut threshold for the variance_threshold operation. Features where the ratio of the most common to second most common value falls below this threshold are removed.

feature_select_unique_cut.description: Unique cut threshold for the variance_threshold operation. Features where fewer than this fraction of values are unique are removed.

feature_select_min_rows_stats.description: Minimum number of rows required to apply statistics-based feature selection operations (variance_threshold, correlation_threshold, drop_outliers, noise_removal). Groups with fewer rows fall back to name-based operations only (blocklist, drop_na_columns), preventing degenerate empty feature lists from tiny groups.

feature_select_outlier_cutoff.description: Absolute-value cutoff for the drop_outliers operation. Features whose maximum absolute value across rows exceeds this threshold are removed. Only used when drop_outliers is included in feature_select_operations.

feature_select_noise_removal_perturb_gro.description: Metadata column identifying replicate groups for the noise_removal operation. The operation drops features whose mean within-group standard deviation exceeds feature_select_noise_removal_stdev_cutoff. Required when noise_removal is included in feature_select_operations; leave unset otherwise.

feature_select_noise_removal_stdev_cutof.description: Mean within-replicate-group standard deviation above which a feature is dropped by the noise_removal operation. Only used when noise_removal is included in feature_select_operations.

feature_select_per_channel_correlation.description: If true and correlation_threshold is in feature_select_operations, run correlation_threshold once per channel group (features sharing the same channel set) instead of once across all features. Reduces over-aggressive deduplication of features that are correlated only because they describe the same channel.

embedding.title: Embedding
embedding.description: Parameters controlling PCA + UMAP embeddings computed per analysis group.

embedding_pca_components.description: Number of PCA components to compute. Capped at runtime to min(n_rows, n_features).

embedding_umap_neighbors.description: UMAP n_neighbors parameter. Capped at runtime to n_rows - 1 for small groups.

sample_max_nan_fraction.description: Per-sample (row) NaN tolerance as a fraction of feature columns, used by the embedding and clustering steps so they use the same samples. Samples above the threshold are dropped; remaining samples have NaNs filled with 0. Default 0.0 drops any sample with a NaN.

embedding_min_rows.description: Minimum number of rows (after NaN filtering) required to compute PCA + UMAP for a group. Groups below this threshold are skipped: a metadata-only parquet is emitted and the summary JSON records skipped=true.

clustering.title: Clustering
clustering.description: Parameters controlling hierarchical clustering computed per analysis group: samples are clustered with Ward linkage on the feature-selected profiles or their PCA embeddings, and features on the feature-selected profiles.

clustering_samples_input.description: Input for sample clustering: 'pcs' clusters the principal components from the embedding step, 'features' clusters the feature-selected profiles (slower for large groups, as clustering time grows with the number of columns).

clustering_samples_distance_metric.description: Distance metric for sample clustering, which always uses Ward linkage. 'cosine' and 'correlation' are implemented by scaling each sample to unit length (after centering it, for correlation) before Ward/euclidean clustering. 'correlation' is recommended only with clustering_samples_input 'features', since centering a sample's PC scores is not meaningful.

clustering_max_samples.description: Maximum number of samples to cluster. Clustering time grows with the square of the number of samples (and linearly with the number of features or PCs clustered), so groups with more rows than this are skipped rather than clustered, and the output JSON records skipped=true.

clustering_features_linkage_method.description: Linkage method for feature clustering, passed to scipy.cluster.hierarchy.linkage. Note: 'ward' requires clustering_features_distance_metric to be 'euclidean'.

clustering_features_distance_metric.description: Distance metric for feature clustering, passed to scipy.cluster.hierarchy.linkage. Note: clustering_features_linkage_method 'ward' requires 'euclidean'.

institutional_config_options.title: Institutional config options
institutional_config_options.description: Parameters used to describe centralised config profiles. These should not be edited.
institutional_config_options.help_text: The centralised nf-core configuration profiles use a handful of pipeline parameters to describe themselves. This information is then printed to the Nextflow log when you run a pipeline. You should not need to change these values when you run a pipeline.

custom_config_version.description: Git commit id for Institutional configs.

custom_config_base.help_text: If you're running offline, Nextflow will not be able to fetch the institutional config files from the internet. If you don't need them, then this is not a problem. If you do need them, you should download the files from the repo and tell Nextflow where to find them with this parameter.

generic_options.title: Generic options
generic_options.description: Less common options for the pipeline, typically set in a config file.
generic_options.help_text:
These options are common to all nf-core pipelines and allow you to customise some of the core preferences for how the pipeline runs.

Typically these options would be set in a Nextflow config file loaded for all pipeline runs, such as `~/.nextflow/config`.

publish_dir_mode.description: Method used to save pipeline results to output directory.
publish_dir_mode.help_text: The Nextflow `publishDir` option specifies which intermediate files should be saved to the output directory. This option tells the pipeline what method should be used to move these files. See [Nextflow docs](https://www.nextflow.io/docs/latest/process.html#publishdir) for details.

email_on_fail.description: Email address for completion summary, only when pipeline fails.
email_on_fail.help_text: An email address to send a summary email to when the pipeline is completed - ONLY sent if the pipeline does not exit successfully.

plaintext_email.description: Send plain-text email instead of HTML.

monochrome_logs.description: Do not use coloured log outputs.

validate_params.description: Boolean whether to validate parameters against the schema at runtime

pipelines_testdata_base_path.description: Base URL or local path to location of pipeline test dataset files

trace_report_suffix.description: Suffix to add to the trace report filename. Default is the date and time in the format yyyy-MM-dd_HH-mm-ss.

help_full.description: Display the full detailed help message.

show_hidden.description: Display hidden parameters in the help message (only works when --help or --help_full are provided).
